svg.title: The flight loop as wm-flight-wiring.edn declares it
svg.text: The flight loop as the wiring map declares it
Generated from holes/labs/M-wm-wiring/wm-flight-wiring.edn (7d73f8cb, futon3c HEAD f5a17980) by spike/wm_wiring_svg.bb; not hand edited. 74 boxes, 52 fields.
Each panel is one step of the flight, in order. A box is a source var the map pins, listing what it writes (w) and reads (r). A field kept inside a step is an arrow inside its panel.

A field that crosses steps is one line in the band below, tapped by its writer (dot) and each reader (arrow). The registered test checks each site at the pins (futon2 ac06a830, futon3c 58f1a8cb), expecting 171 findings (2 to-do). 8 fields cross steps; 4 of 11 steps are entered or left by none.

svg.text: solid box: built component at its pinned var (52)
dashed amber box: declared, not built, drawn at its intended site (1)
dotted box: the step's registered test, a declared reader; it lists its reads and draws no arrows (21)
grey box: siteless component, exempt from conformance (3)
line: a field, from its one writer to its readers, both built (42 reader arrows; 8 fields cross steps, 35 stay inside one)
dashed amber: declared on a box not yet built (6)
purple: the reader is an earlier step than the writer, the loop closing (4)
grey stub: a field read that no box writes (3); green stub: the owner's text, exogenous (1)

Numbered rings: the exemplar trace the map records for M-autoclock-in, in order (loop-entry > r1-outer-cascade > flight-entry > dispatch > clock-in > r2-served-by-reading > r2-verifier > r6-cascade-lane > r9-selection-law > r0-enact-step > r7-flight-call > wc-checker > r7-increment > r7-fold > r1-outer-cascade). Boxes on it have a heavier border.

What this does not show: the prover reads sites textually, so a field's presence at a var is what is checked, not that the value flows; the eleven code shapes it cannot see are listed in WM-MAP-REPLAY-D. Standing findings (169) are generic keys the prover cannot scope per box.
A step marked as entered or left by no field is one whose inputs and outputs the map does not yet declare; that is a gap in the map, not in the drawing.
